# Dimension 2: Claude Code Skills and Commands Architecture

References: [citations.md](../citations.md)

## Architecture Overview

Skills are prompt-based extensions that inject markdown instructions into Claude's conversation context when invoked [5][6]. They operate through **progressive disclosure** — a three-level loading strategy that minimizes context consumption [5]:

| Level | What Loads | When |
|-------|-----------|------|
| 1. Metadata | Name + description of every installed skill | Always (system prompt) |
| 2. Full skill | Complete SKILL.md content | On invocation |
| 3. Supporting files | Referenced .md files, scripts, examples | On-demand via filesystem |

"Agents with a filesystem and code execution tools don't need to read the entirety of a skill into their context window when working on a particular task. This means that the amount of context that can be bundled into a skill is effectively unbounded" [5].

## SKILL.md Format

Skills are directories containing a required `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter and markdown content [6]:

### Frontmatter Fields

| Field | Purpose | Determinism Impact |
|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `name` | Display name, becomes /slash-command | Invocation identity |
| `description` | When to use (250-char cap in listing) | LLM matching accuracy |
| `disable-model-invocation` | Prevent auto-loading by Claude | Eliminates probabilistic triggering |
| `user-invocable` | Show/hide from / menu | User control |
| `allowed-tools` | Tools permitted during skill (CLI only) | Tool access scoping |
| `context` | Set to `fork` for subagent execution | Context isolation |
| `agent` | Subagent type for fork context | Execution environment |
| `model` | Model override | Capability control |
| `effort` | Effort level override | Quality/speed tradeoff |
| `hooks` | Skill-scoped lifecycle hooks | Per-skill deterministic control |
| `paths` | Glob patterns limiting activation | File-type scoping |

Source: [6]

### Dynamic Context Injection

The `` !`command` `` syntax runs shell commands before skill content reaches Claude [6]:

```yaml
## Pull request context
- PR diff: !`gh pr diff`
- PR comments: !`gh pr view --comments`
```

This is preprocessing — Claude sees only the rendered output, not the commands [6].

## Invocation Mechanics

### Who Can Invoke

| Configuration | User (slash) | Claude (auto) | Context Loaded |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------|
| Default | Yes | Yes | Description always; full on invoke |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | Yes | No | Description NOT in context |
| `user-invocable: false` | No | Yes | Description always; full on invoke |

Source: [6]

### Skill Tool as Meta-Tool

The Skill tool is a single tool in Claude's tools array that manages invocation of individual skills [28]. Claude evaluates skill descriptions against the current context to determine relevance [6]. The description budget scales at 1% of context window with an 8,000-character fallback, configurable via `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` [6].

## Commands Merger

Custom commands (`.claude/commands/*.md`) and skills (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) are now a unified system [6]. Both create `/slash-command` interfaces. Skills add optional features: directory for supporting files, frontmatter for invocation control, and auto-loading. Existing `.claude/commands/` files continue working; if both exist with the same name, the skill takes precedence [6].

## Priority Hierarchy

When skills share the same name across levels, higher-priority locations win [6]:

```
enterprise > personal > project
```

Plugin skills use `plugin-name:skill-name` namespace and cannot conflict with other levels [6].

## Code Execution for Determinism

Skills can include executable scripts for operations better suited to code than token generation [5]:

"Large language models excel at many tasks, but certain operations are better suited for traditional code execution. For example, sorting a list via token generation is far more expensive than simply running a sorting algorithm" [5].

"Because code is deterministic, this workflow is consistent and repeatable" [5].

## Cross-Platform Support (Open Standard)

Agent Skills published as an open standard at agentskills.io [18]. As of March 2026, 32 tools/platforms adopt the standard [18], including:

- Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude Agent SDK [5][18]
- Cursor, GitHub Copilot, VS Code Copilot [18]
- Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex [18]
- JetBrains Junie, Kiro (AWS), Databricks, Snowflake [18]
- Goose (Block), Roo Code, Letta, Spring AI [18]
- Mistral Vibe, Laravel Boost, and others [18]

"Originally developed by Anthropic, released as an open standard, and has been adopted by a growing number of agent products" [18].

## Documented Reliability Problems

### CLAUDE.md Instruction Drift

"The current behavior is: 'I read your rules, I understand your rules, I don't follow your rules'" [15].

Cyclic failure pattern documented: bad thing happens → create rule → Claude ignores rule → bad thing repeats → user reminds → Claude apologizes → next session: back to ignoring [15].

At least three GitHub issues document this: #18660, #14417, #7777 [15][24][25].

### Skill Auto-Triggering Failures

One practitioner reported 0/20 skill triggers on prompts that should have activated a skill [26]. Description optimization is the primary mitigation [26].

### Reliability Spectrum (Community Consensus)

Community practitioners rank Claude Code's control mechanisms by reliability [27]:

```
hooks > slash commands > skills > auto-invocation
```

This aligns with the fundamental distinction: hooks execute deterministically, while skills and CLAUDE.md rely on the LLM choosing to follow instructions [7][27][29].

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No enforcement mechanism:** CLAUDE.md and skills are suggestions, not constraints — the model can acknowledge and ignore them [15]
- **Context window degradation:** Instruction adherence degrades over conversation length as positional attention dynamics shift [15][40]
- **Token overhead:** Skill descriptions consume context on every turn; with many skills, this compounds [6]
- **No quantitative reliability data:** The 0/20 trigger rate [26] and "reliability spectrum" [27] are practitioner observations, not controlled measurements
